query: Death Valley Furnace Creek DEVC1 station highest daily maximum temperature recorded so far July 2026, actual observations July 7-13 2026
answer:
I've completed the research on Death Valley Furnace Creek (DEVC1) temperatures for early-mid July 2026.

## Key Findings

**Highest daily maximum in the July 7–13, 2026 window: ~120°F (≈48.9°C), reached around July 9, 2026.**

Daily maxima (observation-blended model, °F):
- July 7: ~116 | July 8: ~118 | **July 9: ~120 (peak)** | July 10: ~120 | July 11: ~120 | July 12: ~113 | July 13: ~107

## Important data caveats
- **Direct DEVC1 gauge data was hard to fully retrieve.** The NWS `api.weather.gov` DEVC1 endpoint only retains ~36 hours of data, so it returned only July 12–13, showing a confirmed **45.06°C (~113°F)**. DEVC1 is a RAWS/cooperative station, absent from standard ASOS archives.
- **Three data sources gave different figures**: the forecast model (obs-blended, ~120°F peak — most realistic for Death Valley), ERA5 reanalysis (cool-biased, 113°F peak), and the truncated direct gauge (113°F for July 12–13, which matches the model's July 12 value).
- **No news coverage** of a record event was found — temperatures were seasonally normal, not near record levels.

## Context
This ~120°F peak is hot but ordinary for Death Valley in July — well below the site's modern extreme highs (~129°F/54°C) and the all-time world record of 134°F (56.7°C) set at Furnace Creek on July 10, 1913.

**Confidence:** The ~120°F July 9 peak is model-derived rather than a directly-confirmed gauge reading; I could not independently verify the exact DEVC1 gauge maximum for July 9 due to the endpoint's short retention window.
